# Background

Your Cuban uncle sets up a cocktail bar in downtown Budapest. He has a secret list of cocktails that he would like to serve in the bar. He asks you to do create a few lists and tables to set up the shop. As your uncle is a secret hipster, he has a dataset on Github that you can use for the task!

![](https://media1.tenor.com/images/57a519cffd0ad4693be3b9c94b211540/tenor.gif?itemid=5195211){width="320"}

Note: There are several different ways to solve these tasks, feel free to come up with your own.

## 1. Read the data

Read the cocktail dataset from: <https://github.com/nthun/cocktail-balance> You can also find the codebook there.

```{r coctail_data, include = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)

coctail_data <- read_tsv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nthun/cocktail-balance/refs/heads/master/cocktail_data.tsv")

view(coctail_data)
```

## 2. Transform the data table and clean the ingredient variable!

The ingredients are currently in a single cell for each cocktail. It would be better to put them in separate rows. Also, the variable should be cleaned of all quantities (e.g. 1/2 oz, 2 dashes, etc.), and the indicator of alcohol content (e.g. 47.3% abv). You will need to use this cleaned table in later tasks.

```{r coctail_clean, include = FALSE}
coctail_clean <- coctail_data %>% 
  separate_longer_delim(cols = ingredients,
                        delim = regex("<br\\s*/?>|<b4\\s*/?>")) %>%
 mutate(
   ingredients = ingredients %>% 
     str_remove("\\(?\\s*[0-9.]+\\s*%\\s*abv\\s*\\)?") %>% 
     str_remove("^[0-9/. ]+(oz|dashes|dash|drops|drop)?\\s*") %>% 
     str_squish()) %>% 

view()

```

## 3. All ingredients in alphabetical order

Before opening the bar, you need to find a reliable supplier that has all the ingredients. You need to send a list of all possible ingredients you will need. They don't need the quantities (i.e. how many of these are needed), just the names of the ingredients.

```{r}
coctail_ingredients_alphabetical <- coctail_clean %>%
  mutate(ingredients = str_to_title(ingredients)) %>%
  select(ingredients) %>%
  distinct(ingredients) %>%
  arrange(ingredients) %>%

view()
```

## 4. Number of unique ingredients

How many different ingredients you will need?

```{r}
n_ingredients <- coctail_ingredients_alphabetical %>%
  count(ingredients) %>%
  summarise(n_unique = n_distinct(ingredients))

print(n_ingredients)

```

## 5. What are the top 10 ingredients?

What are the 10 most frequently used ingredients? If there are ties, you can list more than 10.

```{r}
top_10 <- coctail_clean %>%
  mutate(ingredients = str_to_title(ingredients)) %>%
  count(ingredients, sort = TRUE)  %>% 
  slice_max(n, n = 10, with_ties = TRUE) %>% 

view()
```

## 6. Which cocktail(s) has/have the most ingredients?

Count the number of ingredients and filter all the cocktails that has that many.

```{r}
most_ingredients <- coctail_clean %>% 
  count(name, name = "n_ingredients", sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_max(n_ingredients, n = 1, with_ties = TRUE)
  
view(most_ingredients)
```

## 7. How many ingredients appear in only one cocktail (rare ingredient)? !!44!!

Count all cocktails with only one ingredient, and

```{r}
rare_ingredients <- coctail_clean %>%
  distinct(name, ingredients) %>%
  count(ingredients) %>%
  filter(n == 1)

view(rare_ingredients)

```

## 8. Which cocktail has an ingredient that is only used in one cocktail? !!44!!

```{r}

pairs <- coctail_clean %>%
  distinct(name, ingredients)

unique_ingredients <- pairs %>%
  count(ingredients) %>%
  filter(n == 1)

result <- pairs %>%
  filter(ingredients %in% rare_ingredients$ingredients) %>%
  
view(result)  
```

## 9. What are the cocktails without rare ingredients? !!44!!

```{r}
all_cocktails <- coctail_clean %>%
  distinct(name)

# cocktails that DO have a rare ingredient (from question 8)
cocktails_with_rare <- result %>%
  distinct(name)

# cocktails without rare ingredients
no_rare <- all_cocktails %>%
  anti_join(cocktails_with_rare, by = "name")

view(no_rare)
```

## 10. Create a cheat sheet for the bartender! !!44!!

Create a matrix that shows all cocktail names as rows and all ingredients as columns. When a cocktail requires an ingredient, there should be an "X" in the cell, otherwise, the cell should remain empty. Example:

```{r echo=FALSE}
tribble(~name, ~Lime, ~`White rum`, ~`Cane sugar`, ~`Coca-cola`, ~Mint, ~Soda,
        "Caipirissima", "X", "X", "X", "", "", "",
        "Cuba Libre", "X", "X", "", "X","","",
        "Mojito", "X", "X", "", "", "X", "X") %>% 
    relocate(name, sort(names(.)))
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
cheat_sheet <- coctail_clean %>%
  mutate(ingredients = str_to_sentence(ingredients)) %>%   # consistent capitalisation, like the example
  filter(ingredients != "") %>%                             # drop any empty cells left by the cleaning
  distinct(name, ingredients) %>%                           # one row per cocktail-ingredient pair
  mutate(value = "X") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = ingredients,
              values_from = value,
              values_fill = "") %>%                         # empty cell where the ingredient isn't needed
  select(name, sort(setdiff(names(.), "name")))             # name first, ingredients in alphabetical order

view(cheat_sheet)
```
